source.title: Towards Automated Fact-Checking of Real-World Claims: Exploring Task Formulation and Assessment with LLMs
source.authors: Premtim Sahitaj; Iffat Maab; Junichi Yamagishi; Jawan Kolanowski; Sebastian Möller; Vera Schmitt

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether downstream fact-checking performance changes with model scale, using task accuracy, F1 and justification-quality scores rather than measuring pretraining loss or fitting scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al.'s scaling law in related work, but reports no results on held-out pretraining loss, power-law fits, large-run extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation. Its own results compare AFC performance across Llama model sizes and therefore bear on V6. The example fact-checking prompts are not study findings.
record.test_reason: The study compares one-shot fact-checking accuracy, F1 and TIGERScore across Llama-3 instruct models of 3B, 8B and 70B. It reports a significant model-size effect (Friedman p<0.05), which bears on V6 in a new downstream setting. There is only a size ordering: no pretraining loss, fitted curve or prediction. Sizes are also confounded with model version and token count (3.2 used 9T tokens, 3.1/3.3 used 15T).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Larger Llama models are better at classification and justification quality, evidence retrieval helps all models significantly, and nuanced labels are harder. The authors also conclude that larger models gain more from evidence (significant for TIGERScore only). They find small LLMs match fine-tuned ModernBERT, while larger LLMs surpass it.
record.recipe_differences: The original studies measure language-model pretraining loss and scaling/compute allocation. This paper evaluates instruction-finetuned Llama models on one-shot downstream AFC tasks; it does not conduct a pretraining scaling-law experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported performance varies with evidence inclusion and label granularity. Evidence generally improves classification and justification scores; the paper reports a significant model-size effect on micro F1 and TIGERScore.
record.problems: The scale comparison covers selected instruction-finetuned Llama checkpoints at 3B, 8B and 70B, on one AFC dataset and task. It does not fit a scale curve or report uncertainty for individual table scores; statistical significance is reported for aggregate comparisons. The text describes the 3B model as struggling to outperform the baseline significantly.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted F1 macro and weighted scores from Tables 4–6, and TIGERScore values for the no-evidence settings in Tables 4–6, to stay within the 60-row limit. Accuracy and micro F1 (where distinct) are retained for classification, and TIGERScore is retained for evidence-present settings. For 5-class and 3-class settings, accuracy equals micro F1 in every reported model/condition, so those matching scores are represented once.

untested.parts: Prediction of downstream performance from pretraining loss; any fitted scale-performance curve or extrapolation; sizes beyond 3B–70B; size effects separated from training-token and version differences.
No other modality or regime scaling.

missing.what: Aggregate Friedman test across the four models on micro F1 and TIGERScore, with and without evidence: significant size effect (p<0.05)
Evidence gain vs model size: TIGERScore gains differ significantly across sizes (p<0.05), with larger models gaining more; micro F1 gains do not (p=0.167)
TIGERScore without evidence per model (e.g. 5-class: -3.995, -3.416, -2.554, -2.361), which is also monotonic in size; declared left out in rows_left_out

record.verdict_notes: Weak test of V6: only three sizes, instruction-tuned checkpoints, and size confounded with model generation and training tokens (9T vs 15T). The only Kaplan mention is in related work. Row states were judged against a majority-class baseline, which is not the V6 comparison; the scale trend must be read across rows. Table 6 F1 values are internally inconsistent with accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining-loss measurements or scaling sweeps over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No fits on small runs or predictions of larger-run losses.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or comparison of parameter and token growth.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or training regimes are tested for scaling-law behavior.
Tests downstream AFC performance across selected model sizes, but not prediction from pretraining loss, a fitted scale-performance curve, or downstream tasks beyond this fact-checking setup.
Does not test whether scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits depend on fitting or training choices, or whether loss curves bend.

relationships.condition: Llama-3 instruct 3B→8B→70B, all label schemes, with and without evidence
relationships.reason: Accuracy and TIGERScore rise monotonically with size in every setting, e.g. 5-class accuracy with evidence 0.321→0.339→0.389/0.405 (v6-5c-*-yes-acc). The text reports a significant size effect (Friedman p<0.05).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy and TIGERScore increased monotonically with size, including five-class evidence-based accuracy of 0.321→0.339→0.389/0.405, with a significant size effect at Friedman p<0.05.

relationships.condition: Same parameter count (70B), different checkpoint (Llama-3.1 vs 3.3); and small 3B vs 8B gaps
relationships.reason: At fixed 70B, Llama-3.3 beats Llama-3.1 by about as much as some size steps, so size alone does not predict performance. TIGERScore with evidence is -1.686 vs -2.466 (5-class), -1.884 vs -2.524 (3-class) and -1.739 vs -2.433 (binary). Separately, 3B vs 8B no-evidence accuracy differs only 0.464 vs 0.472 (3-class), and binary 3B no-evidence accuracy (0.504) is at baseline.
relationships.display_finding: At 70B, Llama-3.3 outscored Llama-3.1 on evidence-based TIGERScore across five-class, three-class and binary tasks (−1.686 versus −2.466, −1.884 versus −2.524, and −1.739 versus −2.433); without evidence, three-class accuracy was 0.464 at 3B versus 0.472 at 8B, and 3B binary accuracy of 0.504 was at baseline.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Tested Llama instruction-finetuned models, across the reported AFC label schemes and evidence settings
reader_labels.reason: Classification accuracy/F1 and evidence-setting TIGERScore generally improve with model size in the tested comparisons (rows v6-5c-3b-no-acc through v6-2c-70b3-yes-f1micro and v6-tiger-5c-3b-yes through v6-tiger-2c-70b3-yes). These results show a scale-related downstream performance trend, not a fitted predictive law.
